A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dimensionality-compression learning method. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching the earlier S-numbered appendix material to the later A-numbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, together with ablations, representation analyses, and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a Greedy InfoMax reimplementation, noise-strength and sampling-size experiments, and activation-sparsity measurements.

M1.justification: The convolutional architecture, local ED consistency/diversity objective, noisy input copies, orthonormal projections, and mean-squared-output inference remain unchanged. The FOP modules explicitly depicted in v2 Figure 2 represent projections already described in v1 Section 3 and Appendix S1.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 for image classification. The new experiments vary model settings and analyze existing representations; they introduce no additional dataset, domain, or distinct task.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds reimplemented Greedy InfoMax (GIM) comparisons on all three datasets. The existing BP, DFA, original FF, CaFo FF, CwC FF, Soft Hebbian, Hard Hebbian, and EBL comparators remain.

E3.justification: The main architecture and three-epoch/60-epoch training schedule remain. Added experiments sweep dropout probability from 0.1 to 0.5 and noisy-copy counts from 4 to 20, and measure Hoyer sparsity using 100 samples per class. GIM introduces MNIST resizing to 32×32 and simultaneous block updates. Equation 5 also revises the COS evaluation metric.

E4.justification: Appendix A1.3 adds systematic joint noise-strength and sampling-size sensitivity analyses, while A1.4 adds layerwise activation-sparsity comparisons with and without projection. These investigate previously untested aspects of the proposed mechanism. v2 also reports degradation beyond three convolutional blocks and revises the existing orthogonality analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run evaluations and one-standard-deviation error bars. The new GIM and sparsity results extend this existing reporting practice rather than introduce a new statistical procedure. Tables A2–A4 provide point estimates without a new uncertainty-estimation method.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds GIM accuracies of 99.29 ± 0.03, 78.19 ± 0.34, and 50.09 ± 0.45. Tables A2–A5 add substantial sensitivity and sparsity findings, including CIFAR-100 accuracy of 25.21 at dropout 0.5 with 20 copies. COS curves in Figure 3b and Figure S2/A2 change under the revised metric; these are not headline accuracy gains.

T1.justification: Equation 5 changes mathematically: v1 uses signed cosine similarities with channel-dependent weighting, whereas v2 uniformly averages one minus absolute cosine similarity over channel pairs. The ED objective and information-decomposition mathematics remain equivalent after notation changes, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unsupervised FF learning through ED compression without negative samples, competitive non-BP classification, and beneficial use of noise and mean-squared-output inference. Additional evidence and discussion do not redefine the main algorithmic contribution or introduce a state-of-the-art performance claim.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes compression in projected space from sparsity in the original representation. It replaces the earlier statement that deeper architectures were untested with reported degradation and a class-feature-collapse explanation. Section 5 substantially expands interpretations involving self-supervised learning, predictive coding, and possible WTA/inhibitory biological implementations.

D1.justification: v2 documents GIM script reuse and adaptation, activation-vector construction for sparsity analysis, and supplementary code packaging. Conversely, v1's explicit description of BP's initial end-to-end training is omitted. The proposed model's architecture, optimizer, main hyperparameters, hardware, and repository disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and 5 substantially broaden positioning through GIM and slow-feature learning, Barlow Twins and VICReg, predictive coding, and biological WTA/inhibitory circuits. These additions explain relationships and distinctions beyond the earlier emphasis on FF, EBL, and Hebbian learning.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work narrative, and ED explanation are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Section 3 now introduces ED before the neural-tuning illustration, and projection discussion moves into the training description. Widespread terminology and prose edits accompany the expanded discussion, acknowledgments, and conference checklist.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different conference layout, redraws and expands Figure 1, and adds explicit projection modules to Figure 2. Table 1 is reorganized and expanded, and four new appendix tables are introduced. Existing appendix figures are matched across renumbering and relocation, with updated COS displays distinguished from retained plots.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and provides useful evidence about the method's central noise and projection assumptions through Tables A2–A5. The documented GIM comparison and more explicit depth and sparsity limitations make the contribution easier to assess. These gains are limited by missing per-setting uncertainty in the new sensitivity tables and the absence of quantitative details for the reported deeper-network failures.
